And at this time the fifth king arose in Egypt, Pharaoh Karimon, for four years.
And at this time, Armonis the Canaanite had two sons, Sodom and Gomorrah;
and he built a city named after each one of them.
And he also built Zoar, named after Zoar their mother.
And again there arose the sixth king in Egypt,
Pharaoh Apintos, for thirty-two years.
This man sent to Kesaronos the Parthian king,
and brought the writings and learning of the Chaldeans to Egypt.
And Apintos also built a city upon the river Nile,
and named it Babylon, that is, Babel.
And Asaph also says that in the days of Terah the Egyptians learned Chaldean lore,
and they made a golden image to the idol Kinos.
After [Terah was] seventy {OCR?}
years old, he begot Abraham.
And all his days were two hundred and seventy-five years.
And in the fifth year of Terah, the fifth king arose in Babylon, Arpazad {OCR?}, for eighteen years.
And then the kingdom of Babylon ceased for seven years,
until Belos the Assyrian rebelled against the Chaldeans,
and fought with them and with the Medes, and overcame them.
And he reigned over Assyria, and Babylon, and all Asia except India, for sixty-two years.
And in the fifth year of Terah, the seventh king reigned in Egypt,
Pharaoh Ouronkos,
for thirty-three years.
And after him,
the eighth king, Pharaoh Simonos, for twenty years.
And after him,
the ninth king, Pharaoh Arminos, for twenty-seven years.
And twenty years before Abraham was born, Damascus was built by Murphos.
And Josephus says
